items.title: VRS-Python
items.text:
VRS-Python implements the GA4GH Variation Representation Specification (VRS) in Python. It helps you represent variants consistently and compare records across data sources using identifiers computed from their content.

Use VRS-Python to:

  • Build and validate VRS and GKM-Core objects with Pydantic (see VRS compatibility).
  • Normalize alleles and compute consistent GA4GH identifiers.
  • Translate supported HGVS, SPDI, and gnomAD expressions to VRS.
  • Annotate VCF files with VRS allele identifiers.
  • Store and exchange objects using inline or referenced components.

items.title: Set up SeqRepo and UTA
items.text:
Some VRS operations need external data:

  • SeqRepo provides reference sequences and aliases for validation, coordinate interpretation, and normalization.
  • UTA provides transcript metadata and alignments for HGVS interpretation and mapping.
Workflow Data required Model validation, serialization, identifier computation Usually none; reference sequence validation requires SeqRepo Allele normalization, SPDI/gnomAD translation, VCF annotation Reference sequences and aliases, supplied by SeqRepo HGVS transcript interpretation and mapping Sequence data and, when transcript metadata or alignments are needed, UTA

items.title: Docker Compose
items.text:
Docker Compose sets up SeqRepo REST and UTA, including the SeqRepo dataset. You do not need a separate local SeqRepo installation for this setup.

Install ga4gh.vrs[extras] (see installation) and Docker, then clone this repository:

git clone https://github.com/ga4gh/vrs-python.git
cd vrs-python

Run all Compose commands from the repository root, where docker-compose.yml lives. Create the data volumes and start the services:

docker volume create uta_vol
docker volume create seqrepo_vol
docker compose up

Compose starts three containers:

Service Purpose seqrepo Downloads the 2024-12-20 dataset into seqrepo_vol, then exits seqrepo-rest-service Serves the downloaded sequences at http://localhost:5000 uta Runs the uta_20241220 transcript and alignment database on port 5432, with data in uta_vol
  • The first startup may take 5–15 minutes, depending on your network and host.
  • Allow enough disk space for the datasets. Later startups reuse the downloaded data.
  • If SeqRepo REST starts before the download finishes, follow the missing directory steps.

These commands use Compose v2 (docker compose). If you still use v1, the command is docker-compose; upgrading to v2 is recommended.

items.title: Configure Python clients
items.text:
Set these environment variables so VRS-Python can connect to the services:

export GA4GH_VRS_DATAPROXY_URI='seqrepo+http://localhost:5000/seqrepo'
export UTA_DB_URL='postgresql://anonymous:anonymous@localhost:5432/uta/uta_20241220'

from ga4gh.vrs.dataproxy import create_dataproxy

dp = create_dataproxy()  # Reads GA4GH_VRS_DATAPROXY_URI
print(dp.get_sequence("refseq:NM_000059.4", 0, 20))

The expected sequence is AGAGGCGGAGCCGCTGTGGC.

items.title: Verify the services
items.text:
In another terminal, check that seqrepo-rest-service and uta are running:

docker compose ps

Look for both services with status Up and ports 5000 and 5432 published. The relevant columns should look similar to this (container names and elapsed times may differ):

NAME                                SERVICE                STATUS         PORTS
vrs-python-seqrepo-rest-service-1    seqrepo-rest-service   Up 2 minutes   0.0.0.0:5000->5000/tcp
vrs-python-uta-1                     uta                    Up 2 minutes   0.0.0.0:5432->5432/tcp

The seqrepo download container should exit after completing its work, so it will not appear in the default docker compose ps output. Use docker compose ps --all to see it; a successful download shows Exited (0).

Test the two running services:

curl --write-out '\n' 'http://localhost:5000/seqrepo/1/sequence/refseq:NM_000059.4?end=20'

The sequence request should return AGAGGCGGAGCCGCTGTGGC.

Check UTA with the psql client:

psql -XAt 'postgresql://anonymous:anonymous@localhost:5432/uta' \
  -c 'select count(*) from uta_20241220.transcript'

The query should return a positive transcript count, such as 329090.

items.title: Local SeqRepo
items.text:
A local sequence store avoids REST requests. Use this as an alternative to the Compose-managed SeqRepo volume. Install SeqRepo and prepare its default data directory:

pip install biocommons.seqrepo
sudo mkdir -p /usr/local/share/seqrepo
sudo chown "$USER" /usr/local/share/seqrepo

Choose a dataset listed by seqrepo list-remote-instances, then download it:

seqrepo list-remote-instances
export SEQREPO_VERSION=2024-12-20  # Or a newer available dataset
seqrepo pull -i "$SEQREPO_VERSION"
seqrepo update-latest
export GA4GH_VRS_DATAPROXY_URI='seqrepo+file:///usr/local/share/seqrepo/latest'

See SeqRepo's installation documentation for alternate storage locations.

If a completed download raises a PermissionError when renaming its temporary directory, move it manually. For example:

sudo mv /usr/local/share/seqrepo/2024-12-20._fkuefgd /usr/local/share/seqrepo/2024-12-20
seqrepo update-latest

Replace those paths with the temporary and final paths from your error message.

items.title: Local UTA
items.text: To install UTA locally, follow the instructions in the UTA repository.

items.title: Configuration
items.text:
Setting Purpose GA4GH_VRS_DATAPROXY_URI Read automatically by create_dataproxy() when no explicit uri is supplied UTA_DB_URL HGVS library's UTA connection, including the schema name SEQREPO_URI Read by some notebooks and examples and passed as an explicit uri, overriding GA4GH_VRS_DATAPROXY_URI; uses the same seqrepo+ format

Data-proxy URIs must include the seqrepo+ provider prefix. Supported formats:

  • Local absolute path: seqrepo+file:///usr/local/share/seqrepo/latest
  • Local relative path: seqrepo+:../relative/path/to/seqrepo/latest
  • HTTP service: seqrepo+http://example.org:5000/seqrepo
  • HTTPS service: seqrepo+https://example.org/seqrepo

You must supply a URI or set GA4GH_VRS_DATAPROXY_URI.

items.title: Missing SeqRepo directory
items.text:
If seqrepo-rest-service exits with OSError: Unable to open SeqRepo directory /usr/local/share/seqrepo/2024-12-20, check the download container's logs:

docker compose logs seqrepo

Wait for the download to finish, then start the REST service again:

docker compose up seqrepo-rest-service

You can start services individually this way to isolate a startup failure. To inspect the REST service or UTA logs, run:

docker compose logs seqrepo-rest-service uta

items.title: Port already in use
items.text:
Another PostgreSQL server may already use port 5432. A UTA connection error such as FATAL: role "anonymous" does not exist can mean your client reached that server. Another process may also occupy SeqRepo REST's port 5000.

Check the port with sudo lsof -i :5432 or sudo lsof -i :5000. Choose an unused port; sudo lsof -i :5433, for example, should produce no output if it is free.

In docker-compose.yml, change the first number in the service's port mapping. The first number is the host port; the second is the container port. For example, use 5433:5432 for UTA or 5001:5000 for SeqRepo REST:

# Under the uta service:
ports:
  - 5433:5432

# Under the seqrepo-rest-service service:
ports:
  - 5001:5000

Run docker compose up again and check the new ports with lsof. Update the environment variables to use the new ports:

export UTA_DB_URL='postgresql://anonymous:anonymous@localhost:5433/uta/uta_20241220'
export GA4GH_VRS_DATAPROXY_URI='seqrepo+http://localhost:5001/seqrepo'
export SEQREPO_URI="$GA4GH_VRS_DATAPROXY_URI"

Test using the new host ports:

psql -XAt 'postgresql://anonymous:anonymous@localhost:5433/uta' \
  -c 'select count(*) from uta_20241220.transcript'
curl --write-out '\n' 'http://localhost:5001/seqrepo/1/sequence/refseq:NM_000059.4?end=20'

items.title: Other connection and data errors
items.text:
• UTA role or schema missing: check that the URL reaches the intended UTA container, rather than another PostgreSQL server, and names the installed schema.
  • Unknown sequence or alias: check accession versions, assembly, and whether the dataset contains the requested reference.
  • Invalid data-proxy scheme: include seqrepo+; a bare HTTP URL is insufficient.

items.title: Installing for development
items.text:
Install Python 3.14, available as python3.14, before running make devready.

Fork the GitHub repo, then clone your fork and initialize a development environment:

git clone --recurse-submodules git@github.com:YOUR_GITHUB_ID/vrs-python.git
cd vrs-python
make devready
source venv/3.14/bin/activate

make devready installs development dependencies and pre-commit hooks. For a manually prepared environment, install the development dependencies:

python -m pip install -e '.[tests,lint,docs,extras,notebooks]'

If you already cloned the repo, but forgot to include --recurse-submodules you can run:

git submodule update --init --recursive

Keep the VRS submodule at the commit recorded by this repository when switching branches. Do not update it incidentally while changing documentation or code.

items.title: Set up SeqRepo and UTA
items.text: Depending on the code or notebooks you work on, you may need to configure SeqRepo for reference sequences and UTA for transcript metadata and alignments. See Set up SeqRepo and UTA for setup options and environment variables.

items.title: Install the pre-commit hooks
items.text:
If you installed the development dependencies manually, install the hooks:

pre-commit install

This step is already included in make devready.

items.title: Run the style checks
items.text:
After making your changes, check linting and formatting:

python3 -m ruff check .
python3 -m ruff format --check .

items.title: Run the tests
items.text:
Add focused tests for changed behavior, then run the test suite:

python3 -m pytest

The test suite includes VRS compliance tests from the submodule. For direct pytest runs, set the SeqRepo path and use recorded network responses, as CI does:

SEQREPO_ROOT_DIR=tests/data/seqrepo/latest python3 -m pytest --vcr-record=none

items.title: Build and preview the documentation
items.text:
Edit the documentation sources:

  • Markdown pages in docs.
  • API docstrings in src.
  • Notebooks in notebooks/getting_started.

The build generates docs-build and site. Do not edit or commit these directories.

Build the documentation with strict checks before opening a pull request:

make docs

To preview the documentation locally:

make docs-serve

Open http://127.0.0.1:8000. After editing source pages or notebooks, stop the server and rerun the preview command to refresh the staged documentation.

items.title: Open a pull request
items.text:
Run the checks relevant to your changes, review the generated documentation, and open a pull request on GitHub against main. Include a short summary of the change and any relevant testing or documentation notes.

  • Use Closes #123 to close an issue automatically when the pull request merges.
  • Use Refs #123 or link the issue in GitHub for related issues that remain open.

items.title: Installation
items.text:
VRS-Python requires Python 3.11 or later. Install it in a virtual environment:

python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate
python -m pip install ga4gh.vrs

The base package supports model validation, serialization, and identifier computation.

items.title: Translation, local sequence access, and VCF annotation
items.text: Install extras for SeqRepo, UTA, HGVS support, and VCF annotation.

items.title: Prerequisites
items.text: Install the prerequisites for your platform:

items.title: macOS
items.text:
With Homebrew installed, run:

brew update
brew install libpq
brew install python3
brew install postgresql@14

items.title: Ubuntu
items.text: sudo apt install gcc libpq-dev python3-dev

items.title: Install the extras
items.text:
In your virtual environment, run:

python -m pip install 'ga4gh.vrs[extras]'

Sequence and transcript datasets require separate setup:

  • Set up SeqRepo for allele normalization, SPDI/gnomAD translation, and VCF annotation.
  • Set up UTA for HGVS workflows that need transcript metadata or alignments.
  • Model construction, serialization, and identifier computation can run without either service; reference sequence validation requires SeqRepo.

Follow Set up SeqRepo and UTA for configuration instructions.

items.title: Notebooks
items.text:
The notebooks group includes dependencies for running the example notebooks. Include extras for the translation and sequence-access examples:

python -m pip install 'ga4gh.vrs[extras,notebooks]'

items.title: Quick start
items.text:
Build a VRS allele, compute its identifier, and translate between HGVS and VRS.

  • Build and identify: uses SeqRepo to resolve a reference sequence accession.
  • Translate HGVS: also configures UTA for transcript metadata and alignments.

Identifier computation itself does not require an external service.

items.title: Build and identify an allele
items.text:
Before running this example:

  1. Install extras.
  2. Start SeqRepo.

Create an allele for NC_000019.10:g.44908684T>C:

from ga4gh.core import ga4gh_identify
from ga4gh.vrs import models
from ga4gh.vrs.dataproxy import create_dataproxy

dp = create_dataproxy("seqrepo+http://localhost:5000/seqrepo")

# Resolve the RefSeq accession to a RefGet accession.
refget_accession = dp.derive_refget_accession("NC_000019.10")
if refget_accession is None:
    raise ValueError("NC_000019.10 was not found in the SeqRepo dataset")

allele = models.Allele(
    # Reference sequence and interval to replace.
    location=models.SequenceLocation(
        sequenceReference=models.SequenceReference(
            refgetAccession=refget_accession
        ),
        # Zero-based, inter-residue coordinates spanning residue 44908684.
        start=44908683,
        end=44908684,
    ),
    state=models.LiteralSequenceExpression(sequence="C"),  # Replacement sequence.
)

Compute the identifier and print the allele as JSON:

identifier = ga4gh_identify(allele)
print(identifier)
print(allele.model_dump_json(exclude_none=True, indent=2))

The identifier is:

ga4gh:VA.NsWfIPdbQ9LWo4Z5f9lIhMW87kZCtrEc

In the JSON, id is the GA4GH identifier, digest is its digest component, and type names the VRS object type:

{
  "id": "ga4gh:VA.NsWfIPdbQ9LWo4Z5f9lIhMW87kZCtrEc",
  "type": "Allele",
  "digest": "NsWfIPdbQ9LWo4Z5f9lIhMW87kZCtrEc",
  "location": {
    "type": "SequenceLocation",
    "digest": "bqt0x0LbTvEpKXw2x7cUfww7mI_Q_pZJ",
    "sequenceReference": {
      "type": "SequenceReference",
      "refgetAccession": "SQ.IIB53T8CNeJJdUqzn9V_JnRtQadwWCbl"
    },
    "start": 44908683,
    "end": 44908684
  },
  "state": {
    "type": "LiteralSequenceExpression",
    "sequence": "C"
  }
}

items.title: Translate HGVS to VRS
items.text:
Start UTA before running this example.

Configure UTA and create a translator with the data proxy from above:

import os

os.environ["UTA_DB_URL"] = "postgresql://anonymous:anonymous@localhost:5432/uta/uta_20241220"

from ga4gh.vrs.extras.translator import AlleleTranslator

translator = AlleleTranslator(dp)

Translate the same HGVS expression. By default, translation normalizes the allele and computes its identifier:

allele = translator.to_vrs("NC_000019.10:g.44908684T>C", fmt="hgvs")
print(allele.model_dump_json(exclude_none=True, indent=2))

The allele and its identifier match the first example. Translation also assigns an id to the location:

{
  "id": "ga4gh:VA.NsWfIPdbQ9LWo4Z5f9lIhMW87kZCtrEc",
  "type": "Allele",
  "digest": "NsWfIPdbQ9LWo4Z5f9lIhMW87kZCtrEc",
  "location": {
    "id": "ga4gh:SL.bqt0x0LbTvEpKXw2x7cUfww7mI_Q_pZJ",
    "type": "SequenceLocation",
    "digest": "bqt0x0LbTvEpKXw2x7cUfww7mI_Q_pZJ",
    "sequenceReference": {
      "type": "SequenceReference",
      "refgetAccession": "SQ.IIB53T8CNeJJdUqzn9V_JnRtQadwWCbl"
    },
    "start": 44908683,
    "end": 44908684
  },
  "state": {
    "type": "LiteralSequenceExpression",
    "sequence": "C"
  }
}

items.title: Translate back to HGVS
items.text:
from_vrs returns a list because a sequence can have multiple accessions. By default, it uses RefSeq accessions in your SeqRepo dataset:

hgvs_expressions = translator.from_vrs(allele, fmt="hgvs")
print(hgvs_expressions)

The result includes the original expression; other entries depend on your dataset:

['NC_000019.10:g.44908684T>C']

See the translation API for options or explore the notebooks for more examples.

items.title: API reference
items.text:
Install ga4gh.vrs[extras] for translation, HGVS utilities, and VCF annotation.

  • GKM-Core models: Create and validate GKM-Core objects.
  • VRS models: Create and validate VRS objects.
  • Identifiers and digests: Compute identifiers and digests for VRS objects.
  • Normalization: Normalize equivalent allele descriptions to a consistent representation.
  • Data proxies: Retrieve sequences, translate aliases, and validate sequence data.
  • Translation and HGVS: Convert variant descriptions to and from VRS.
  • Object references and storage: Replace nested objects with references, resolve references, and store objects.
  • VCF annotation: Annotate VCF records with VRS allele identifiers from Python.
  • VRS annotate: Annotate VCF files with VRS allele identifiers from the command line.

items.text:
Bases: str, Enum

The logical relationship between concepts in the set, in the context of some knowledge reported about them.

The value 'AND' indicates that the concepts are dependent and occur together in this context - i.e. the reported assertion is not necessarily true for each concept on its own - only in combination with the other(s). The value 'OR' indicates that each concept applies independently in this context - i.e. the reported assertion is necessarily true for each concept on its own, independent of the presence of the other(s).

items.title: iriReference
items.text:

items.title: Identifiers and digests
items.text:
Serialize, digest, and identify GA4GH models.

For an Allele without cached IDs or digests, the main steps are (intermediate helper calls omitted)::

ga4gh_identify(allele)
+ allele.compute_ga4gh_identifier()
  + allele.compute_digest()
    + allele.ga4gh_serialize()
      + location.get_or_create_digest()  # identifiable child
      + state.ga4gh_serialize()          # inline value object
    + encode_canonical_json(...)
    + sha512t24u(...)

Given an Allele, call the public helpers::

from ga4gh.core import ga4gh_digest, ga4gh_identify, ga4gh_serialize

identifier = ga4gh_identify(allele, in_place="never")  # GA4GH CURIE
digest = ga4gh_digest(allele)  # digest component
serialized = ga4gh_serialize(allele)  # canonical JSON bytes

in_place="never" leaves the ID unchanged; "always" stores the result; "default" stores it only when the ID is None. Digests may still be cached.

To reuse any nonempty ID::

from ga4gh.core import VrsObjectIdentifierIs, use_ga4gh_compute_identifier_when

with use_ga4gh_compute_identifier_when(VrsObjectIdentifierIs.MISSING):
    identifier = ga4gh_identify(allele)

GA4GH_INVALID instead requires an ID matching the GA4GH pattern. ANY always calls the model identifier method, which may reuse cached IDs or digests. After editing an allele, refresh changed identifiable children first, then::

identifier = allele.get_or_create_ga4gh_identifier(
    in_place="always", recompute=True
)

ga4gh digest algorithm

Source: sha512t24u from biocommons.seqrepo https://journals.plos.org/plosone/article?id=10.1371/journal.pone.0239883

items.text:
Bases: IntEnum

Control when ga4gh_identify calls the model identifier method.

  • ANY: Always call the method (default).
  • GA4GH_INVALID: Call it when the ID is missing or syntactically invalid.
  • MISSING: Call it only when the ID is None or empty.

The default policy calls the model identifier method. That method may reuse an existing valid identifier or digest; this policy does not force recomputation. Where the source of inputs to ga4gh_identify are well controlled, for example when annotating a VCF file with VRS IDs, using MISSING can improve performance.

This function has three options for in_place editing of vro.id:

items.title: Normalization
items.text:
Normalize alleles before computing identifiers so equivalent indel descriptions produce consistent results. Normalization requires sequence data.

Normalize VRS objects.

Allele normalization validates bounds, trims shared sequence, expands repeat ambiguity, and chooses a literal or reference-length expression. Substitutions and identity alleles return before expansion.

For reference CAAAG, inserting A inside the run expands as follows::

input:    [2, 2), literal "A"
expanded: [1, 4), reference "AAA", alternate "AAAA"
output:   ReferenceLengthExpression(length=4, repeatSubunitLength=1)

A substitution needs only trimming: ACGT -> ATGT at [0, 4) becomes C -> T at [1, 2), with a LiteralSequenceExpression.

Given an inline literal Allele and a data proxy serving its reference::

from ga4gh.vrs import normalize

compact = normalize(allele, data_proxy, rle_seq_limit=0)
with_sequence = normalize(allele, data_proxy, rle_seq_limit=None)

0 omits the optional RLE sequence; None retains it without a length limit. A positive limit retains the complete sequence only if it fits. Use the original literal input for each call: existing RLE states are returned unchanged.

See https://vrs.ga4gh.org/en/stable/impl-guide/normalization.html

items.title: Object references and storage
items.text:
Convert VRS objects between inline objects and identifier references.

Given an Allele with an inline SequenceLocation::

from ga4gh.vrs import vrs_deref, vrs_enref

store = {}
allele_id, referenced = vrs_enref(allele, store, return_id_obj_tuple=True)
restored = vrs_deref(referenced, store)

The round trip is::

allele.location       -> SequenceLocation(...)
referenced.location   -> "ga4gh:SL.<digest>"
store[allele_id]       -> referenced Allele
restored.location     -> stored SequenceLocation

Both operations copy the top-level input. Dereferencing inserts store values directly, so resolving nested references can mutate those stored objects.

Convert ga4gh objects between inlined and referenced forms.

Referable attributes are those that may be either an object or CURIE.

These functions require a "class referable attribute" map, which will typically be generated from the schema by pydantic_class_refatt_map() in .models.py.

items.title: Translation and HGVS
items.text:
Translates various external formats into VRS models.

Input formats: VRS (serialized), hgvs, spdi, gnomad (vcf) Output formats: hgvs and spdi for Alleles; no copy-number exporters.

Convert HGVS expressions and coordinates.

HGVS uses 1-based positions; VRS uses interbase bounds. Omitting the accession::

HGVS                            VRS start        VRS end
g.100A>T                        99               100
g.100_101insT                    100              100
g.(100_110)_(200_210)del          Range([99,109])  Range([200,210])

Insertions use the boundary after the start residue for both bounds. For ranges, starts shift by one and ends stay unchanged. AlleleTranslator rejects uncertain ranges; use CnvTranslator for uncertain del/dup copy-number expressions.

With a configured data_proxy and accessible UTA database::

from ga4gh.vrs.extras.translator import AlleleTranslator

translator = AlleleTranslator(data_proxy)
try:
    allele = translator.from_hgvs("NC_000019.10:g.44908822C>T")
    expressions = translator.to_hgvs(allele, namespace="refseq")
finally:
    translator.hgvs_tools.close()  # Closes UTA, not the supplied data proxy.

Coding coordinates pass through c_to_n on import and n_to_c on export.

Generate a list of SPDI expressions for VRS Allele.

If namespace is not None, returns SPDI strings for the specified namespace.

If namespace is None, returns SPDI strings for all alias translations.

If ref_seq_limit is specified, the reference sequence is included in the SPDI expression only if its length is at most the limit. Otherwise only the length of the reference sequence is included. If the limit is None, the reference sequence is always included. In all cases, the alt sequence is included. Default is 0 (never include reference sequence).

SPDI and VRS use identical normalization. The incoming Allele is expected to be normalized per VRS spec.

items.title: VCF annotation
items.text:
Annotate VCFs with VRS identifiers and attributes.

The main processing path is::

annotate(...)
+ for each record: _get_vrs_data(...)
  + for each allele: _get_vrs_object(...)
    + AlleleTranslator.from_gnomad(...)
    + on_vrs_object(...)             # return an allele or None
+ on_vrs_object_collection(...)       # when collection is enabled

For example, keep only alleles with literal states::

from pathlib import Path
from ga4gh.vrs.extras.annotator.vcf import VcfAnnotator
from ga4gh.vrs.models import Allele, LiteralSequenceExpression


class LiteralStateAnnotator(VcfAnnotator):
    def on_vrs_object(
        self, vcf_coords: str, vrs_allele: Allele, **kwargs: object
    ) -> Allele | None:
        if isinstance(vrs_allele.state, LiteralSequenceExpression):
            return vrs_allele
        return None


# data_proxy must serve the input VCF's reference assembly.
LiteralStateAnnotator(data_proxy).annotate(
    Path("input.vcf"), output_ndjson_path=Path("literal-alleles.ndjson")
)

A pickle or NDJSON output enables VcfAnnotator's collection hook. Returning None excludes the allele from collection. If writing a VCF, its record remains with missing annotation values. Per-record errors are logged and written to VRS_Error.

items.text:
get_or_create_ga4gh_identifier(
    in_place: str = "default",
    recompute: bool = False,
    as_version: PrevVrsVersion | None = None,
) -> str

Get a GA4GH computed identifier and optionally update the object ID.

This function has three options for in_place editing of vro.id:

  • 'default': the standard identifier update behavior for GA4GH identifiable objects, this mode will update the vro.id field only when it is None
  • 'always': this will update the vro.id field any time the identifier is computed

items.text:
get_or_create_ga4gh_identifier(
    in_place: str = "default",
    recompute: bool = False,
    as_version: PrevVrsVersion | None = None,
) -> str

Get a GA4GH computed identifier and optionally update the object ID.

This function has three options for in_place editing of vro.id:

  • 'default': the standard identifier update behavior for GA4GH identifiable objects, this mode will update the vro.id field only when it is None
  • 'always': this will update the vro.id field any time the identifier is computed
  • 'never': the vro.id field will not be edited in-place, even when empty

recompute applies when this call computes an identifier. A valid existing ID returned by the default policy bypasses digest computation. An invalid existing ID is replaced in the return value, but is only stored with the always policy.

If as_version is provided, other parameters are ignored and an identifier is returned following the conventions of the VRS version indicated by as_version.

items.title: VRS annotate
items.text:
Use vrs-annotate to annotate input files with VRS variation objects:

vrs-annotate --help

items.title: VCF
items.text:
Install ga4gh.vrs[extras] and configure SeqRepo. Then annotate a VCF with VRS allele identifiers:

vrs-annotate vcf \
  --dataproxy-uri='seqrepo+http://localhost:5000/seqrepo' \
  --assembly=GRCh38 \
  --vcf-out=out.vcf.gz \
  input.vcf.gz

Set --assembly to the input VCF's reference assembly. Set the data-proxy URI with --dataproxy-uri or GA4GH_VRS_DATAPROXY_URI. The command-line option overrides the environment variable.

For available options and defaults:

vrs-annotate vcf --help

To annotate from Python, see the VCF annotation API.

items.title: Explore with notebooks
items.text:
The walkthroughs below are rendered examples, so you can read them directly in your browser without installing anything. They demonstrate how to use VRS-Python to build variation models, compute identifiers, translate variant descriptions, and access sequence data. You can also download a notebook from its page and run it in Jupyter. Pages show saved outputs, which may differ from a fresh run against your installed release and configured data services.

Notebook What you will learn Quick start Translate a variant using sequence services SeqRepo data proxy Retrieve sequences and resolve aliases Basic models Build alleles and compute identifiers Allele translator Translate supported variant nomenclatures CNV translator Represent copy number variation Upcoming features Explore development examples, subject to change Uncertain HGVS ranges Work with uncertain coordinates

Data access

Some notebooks use public demonstration endpoints for sequence and transcript data. These endpoints are intended for exploring the examples. For heavy workloads or production use, we recommend running your own local services. Follow SeqRepo and UTA to set them up, then update the notebooks to use your endpoints. Inspect setup cells before running them, since they may override environment variables you set in the shell.

items.title: Run the notebooks with MyBinder
items.text:
Binder provides a ready-to-use computing environment for running the notebooks directly in your browser, with no local installation required.

You can launch the notebooks on Binder here.

Once launched, select VRS_kernel as the notebook kernel.

items.title: Run the notebooks locally
items.text:
Clone the VRS-Python repository, then follow the Installation steps to create the virtual environment (venv) and activate it.

Notebook dependency

If you did not install the notebooks optional dependency during setup, run this command from the root of the cloned project (vrs-python/), with the virtual environment activated:

python3 -m pip install "ga4gh.vrs[extras,notebooks]"

items.title: Open a notebook
items.text: We recommend either of the following options for opening a notebook.

items.title: JupyterLab
items.text:
1. In the terminal, activate the project's venv virtual environment:

     source venv/bin/activate

  2. In the activated virtual environment, start JupyterLab:

     python3 -m jupyterlab

  3. JupyterLab usually opens automatically in a new browser window. If it does not, open the URL shown in the terminal.

  4. Open a notebook from the notebooks/ directory.

items.title: VS Code
items.text:
1. Install the Python extension and Jupyter extension.
  2. Open the project root in VS Code and open a notebook from the notebooks/ directory.
  3. Select Select Kernel in the upper-right corner and choose the Python interpreter from the repository's venv virtual environment.

items.title: 1. Quick Start
items.text:
This notebook provides instructions on how to get your vrs-python environment up and running with as few steps as possible, and to provide some rudimentary examples to prove it is working properly.

This assumes that you have successfully performed the pre-requisite installations and setup steps detailed in README.md.

The vrs-python package has a dependency on the biocommons seqrepo package. SeqRepo is used for referencing biological sequences. In this series of notebooks we will be using the publicly available SeqRepo when initializing DataProxy as seen below in Step 1:

seqrepo_rest_service_url = "seqrepo+https://services.genomicmedlab.org/seqrepo"

Another dependency of vrs-python is the biocommons hgvs package for parsing HGVS nomenclature. The hgvs package further relies on the biocommons uta package. The Universal Transcript Archive (UTA) is a Postgres database that stores transcripts aligned to sequence references. When necessary, we will define UTA_DB_URL in the environment using the public access version as follows:

UTA_DB_URL="postgresql://anonymous:anonymous@uta.biocommons.org:5432/uta/uta_20210129b"

NOTE The external sources for the SeqRepo and UTA repositories are ONLY to be used as part of this notebook series and are not meant for use in production code. Please refer to the links above and follow the directions provided on how to setup local instances.

items.title: Step 1 - Setup Data Proxy Access
items.text:
The DataProxy provides access to sequence references.

In [1]
from ga4gh.vrs.dataproxy import create_dataproxy
seqrepo_rest_service_url = "seqrepo+https://services.genomicmedlab.org/seqrepo"
seqrepo_dataproxy = create_dataproxy(uri=seqrepo_rest_service_url)

Assert that the UTA URL is defined in the environment

In [2]
import os
os.environ["UTA_DB_URL"] = "postgresql://anonymous:anonymous@uta.biocommons.org:5432/uta/uta_20241220"

items.title: Step 2 - Setup an Allele Translator
items.text:
Now we will create and utilize an AlleleTranslator to test that our setup is good. The AlleleTranslator has the ability to translate single nucleotide variants and simple insertions/deletions forms to VRS. Notice the AlleleTranslator dependency on the DataProxy.

In [3]
from ga4gh.vrs.extras.translator import AlleleTranslator
translator = AlleleTranslator(data_proxy=seqrepo_dataproxy)

items.title: Step 3 - Translate variation representations to VRS
items.text:
Now we are ready to have the AlleleTranslator transform our first SPDI variant representation to VRS. This variant can be viewed in Clinvar

In [4]
vrs_from_spdi = translator.to_vrs("NC_000005.10:80656509:C:TT", "spdi")
vrs_from_spdi.model_dump(exclude_none=True)

Output:

{'id': 'ga4gh:VA.LK_4rOVxyEwrEpaOVd-BDFV0ocbO5vgV',
 'type': 'Allele',
 'digest': 'LK_4rOVxyEwrEpaOVd-BDFV0ocbO5vgV',
 'location': {'id': 'ga4gh:SL.nA5-KovovkH-5p3LF1657nkkeWFwrInI',
  'type': 'SequenceLocation',
  'digest': 'nA5-KovovkH-5p3LF1657nkkeWFwrInI',
  'sequenceReference': {'type': 'SequenceReference',
   'refgetAccession': 'SQ.aUiQCzCPZ2d0csHbMSbh2NzInhonSXwI'},
  'start': 80656509,
  'end': 80656510},
 'state': {'type': 'LiteralSequenceExpression', 'sequence': 'TT'}}

The output above is the JSON structure of an Allele in VRS form. You should be able to recognize the Allele, SequenceLocation, SequenceReference and LiteralSequenceLocation classes.

Now we will pass the HGVS variant representation of the same variant to the AlleleTranslator.

In [5]
vrs_from_hgvs = translator.to_vrs("NC_000005.10:g.80656510delinsTT", "hgvs")
vrs_from_hgvs.model_dump(exclude_none=True)

Output:

{'id': 'ga4gh:VA.LK_4rOVxyEwrEpaOVd-BDFV0ocbO5vgV',
 'type': 'Allele',
 'digest': 'LK_4rOVxyEwrEpaOVd-BDFV0ocbO5vgV',
 'location': {'id': 'ga4gh:SL.nA5-KovovkH-5p3LF1657nkkeWFwrInI',
  'type': 'SequenceLocation',
  'digest': 'nA5-KovovkH-5p3LF1657nkkeWFwrInI',
  'sequenceReference': {'type': 'SequenceReference',
   'refgetAccession': 'SQ.aUiQCzCPZ2d0csHbMSbh2NzInhonSXwI'},
  'start': 80656509,
  'end': 80656510},
 'state': {'type': 'LiteralSequenceExpression', 'sequence': 'TT'}}

The VRS variant representations should be the same.

In [6]
assert(vrs_from_hgvs == vrs_from_spdi)

items.title: Step 1 - Setup Data Proxy Access

from ga4gh.vrs.dataproxy import create_dataproxy

items.title: Step 2 - Information on refseq accessions
items.text:
It is often necessary when building SequenceLocation objects, to obtain the refget accession from a public accession identifier. The DataProxy method derive_refget_accession can do this for you.

In [2]
seqrepo_dataproxy.derive_refget_accession('refseq:NM_002439.5')

Output:

'SQ.Pw3Ch0x3XWD6ljsnIfmk_NERcZCI9sNM'

The DataProxy get_metadata method provides metadata information on the accession including: the date the accession was added, aliases for the accession and reference length.

In [3]
seqrepo_dataproxy.get_metadata("refseq:NM_000551.3")

Output:

{'added': '2016-08-24T05:03:11Z',
 'aliases': ['MD5:215137b1973c1a5afcf86be7d999574a',
  'NCBI:NM_000551.3',
  'refseq:NM_000551.3',
  'SEGUID:T12L0p2X5E8DbnL0+SwI4Wc1S6g',
  'SHA1:4f5d8bd29d97e44f036e72f4f92c08e167354ba8',
  'VMC:GS_v_QTc1p-MUYdgrRv4LMT6ByXIOsdw3C_',
  'sha512t24u:v_QTc1p-MUYdgrRv4LMT6ByXIOsdw3C_',
  'ga4gh:SQ.v_QTc1p-MUYdgrRv4LMT6ByXIOsdw3C_'],
 'alphabet': 'ACGT',
 'length': 4560}

identifier = "ga4gh:SQ.v_QTc1p-MUYdgrRv4LMT6ByXIOsdw3C_"

'CCTCGCCTCCGTTACAACGGCCTACGGTGCTGGAGGATCCTTCTGCGCACG'

items.title: 3. Basic Models
items.text: This notebook details how to compose VRS objects using component classes, not by use of a nomenclature string (HGVS/SPDI/Gnomad-VCF).

items.title: Step 1 - Setup Data Proxy Access
items.text:
The DataProxy provides access to sequence references.

In [1]
from ga4gh.vrs.dataproxy import create_dataproxy
seqrepo_rest_service_url = "seqrepo+https://services.genomicmedlab.org/seqrepo"
seqrepo_dataproxy = create_dataproxy(uri=seqrepo_rest_service_url)

items.title: Step 2 - Access the VRS models package
items.text:
The models package contains the various classes necessary for building VRS objects.

In [2]
from ga4gh.vrs import models

items.title: Step 3 - Build the Allele
items.text:
In this example we are going to build a VRS object from the variant "NC_000005.10:g.80656510delinsTT". This variant can be viewed in Clinvar.

Start by getting the VRS string representation of the sequence reference using the DataProxy object.

In [3]
refget_accession = seqrepo_dataproxy.derive_refget_accession('refseq:NM_002439.5')
print(refget_accession)

Output:

SQ.Pw3Ch0x3XWD6ljsnIfmk_NERcZCI9sNM

Build a dictionary of type SequenceReference containing the refget_accession. Then continue in succession building dictionaries of type SequenceLocation, LiteralSequenceExpression and Allele referencing previously built structures where applicable.

In [4]
sequence_reference_dict = {
    "type": "SequenceReference",
    "refgetAccession": refget_accession
}

sequence_location_dict = {
    "type": "SequenceLocation",
    "sequenceReference": sequence_reference_dict,
    "start": 80656509,
    "end": 80656510
}

literal_sequence_expression_dict = {
    "type": "LiteralSequenceExpression",
    "sequence": "TT"
}

allele_dict = {
    "type": "Allele",
    "location": sequence_location_dict,
    "state": literal_sequence_expression_dict
}
allele = models.Allele(**allele_dict)
allele.model_dump(exclude_none=True)

Output:

{'type': 'Allele',
 'location': {'type': 'SequenceLocation',
  'sequenceReference': {'type': 'SequenceReference',
   'refgetAccession': 'SQ.Pw3Ch0x3XWD6ljsnIfmk_NERcZCI9sNM'},
  'start': 80656509,
  'end': 80656510},
 'state': {'type': 'LiteralSequenceExpression', 'sequence': 'TT'}}

The Allele object is displayed above. Since it was built from component dictionaries, it is not yet complete as not all the identifiable objects have VRS identifiers. Note that not all objects in the Allele object are VRS identifiable.

In [5]
def is_identifiable(obj):
    print(obj.__class__.__name__, "identifiable?", obj.is_ga4gh_identifiable())
sequence_reference = models.SequenceReference(**sequence_reference_dict)
is_identifiable(sequence_reference)
sequence_location = models.SequenceLocation(**sequence_location_dict)
is_identifiable(sequence_location)
literal_sequence_expression = models.LiteralSequenceExpression(**literal_sequence_expression_dict)
is_identifiable(literal_sequence_expression)
is_identifiable(allele)

Output:

SequenceReference identifiable? False
SequenceLocation identifiable? True
LiteralSequenceExpression identifiable? False
Allele identifiable? True

items.title: Step 4 - Compute the identifiers
items.text:
To make the Allele object a valid VRS object - that is that all identifiable objects have valid VRS identifiers - is to use the ga4gh_identify method on the identifiable objects (SequenceLocation, and Allele).

In [6]
from ga4gh.core import ga4gh_identify
allele.location.id = ga4gh_identify(allele.location)
allele.id = ga4gh_identify(allele)
allele.model_dump(exclude_none=True)

Output:

allele = allele_translator.to_vrs("NC_000005.10:g.80656489C>T", "hgvs")
allele.model_dump(exclude_none=True)

Output:

{'id': 'ga4gh:VA.ebezGL6HoAhtGJyVnB_mE5BH18ntKev4',

 'digest': 'ebezGL6HoAhtGJyVnB_mE5BH18ntKev4',

items.title: 5. Exploring the CnvTranslator
items.text: The vrs-python model supports two classes of copy number variation: * CopyNumberChange - an assessment of loss or gain relative to a location within a system, where loss or gain is represented by the following EMBL-EBI Experimental Factor Ontology (EFO) codes: * EFO:0030064 - regional base ploidy * EFO:0030067 - loss * EFO:0030068 - low-level loss * EFO:0030069 - complete genomic loss * EFO:0030070 - gain * EFO:0030071 - low level gain * EFO:0030072 - high-level gain * EFO:0020073 - high-level loss * CopyNumberCount - an absolute count of discrete copies of a location within a gene or system For the CnvTranslator, only HGVS nomenclature is used to describe the variation.

items.title: 7. Translating Uncertain-Range HGVS Expressions
items.text:
ClinVar often reports copy-number variants (CNVs) with imprecise breakpoints, written in HGVS as nested parenthesized ranges:

  • Balanced uncertainty on both sides: g.(A_B)_(C_D)del — the left breakpoint is somewhere between positions A and B (inclusive); the right breakpoint is somewhere between C and D.
  • One-sided unknown: g.(?_N)_(M_?)del — the outer bound on one side is unknown.

VRS 2.x represents this directly: SequenceLocation.start / end can be a Range (a 2-element list of integers, with None allowed for ?) rather than a single int. This notebook walks through parsing the ClinVar expressions from biocommons/hgvs#225 via CnvTranslator, and round-tripping a VRS object with a Range location back to HGVS via AlleleTranslator.

Requirements: hgvs>=2.0.0a0 (which parses uncertain-range expressions). The reverse from_hgvs path for AlleleTranslator intentionally raises ValueError for uncertain ranges, since LiteralSequenceExpression cannot represent an unknown reference; use CnvTranslator for those del/dup cases.

items.title: Setup
items.text:
We use a SeqRepo data proxy (local or REST) and a UTA connection for the HGVS library. Substitute your own URIs as needed.

In [1]
import os

os.environ.setdefault(
    "UTA_DB_URL",
    "postgresql://anonymous:anonymous@uta.biocommons.org:5432/uta/uta_20241220",
)

from ga4gh.vrs import models
from ga4gh.vrs.dataproxy import create_dataproxy
from ga4gh.vrs.extras.translator import AlleleTranslator, CnvTranslator

seqrepo_uri = os.environ.get(
    "SEQREPO_URI", "seqrepo+https://services.genomicmedlab.org/seqrepo"
)
dp = create_dataproxy(uri=seqrepo_uri)
cnv_tlr = CnvTranslator(data_proxy=dp, default_assembly_name="GRCh38", identify=True)
allele_tlr = AlleleTranslator(
    data_proxy=dp, default_assembly_name="GRCh38", identify=True
)

items.title: Example 1 — Balanced uncertain range (dup)
items.text:
ClinVar variation 251062 on GRCh37:

NC_000019.9:g.(11211022_11213339)_(11217364_11218067)dup

The left breakpoint is somewhere in [11211022, 11213339] and the right is somewhere in [11217364, 11218067]. The resulting SequenceLocation carries a Range for both start and end.

In [2]
cnc = cnv_tlr.to_vrs(
    "NC_000019.9:g.(11211022_11213339)_(11217364_11218067)dup", "hgvs"
)
cnc.model_dump(exclude_none=True)

Output:

  'type': 'SequenceLocation',
  'digest': 'ZFKeEaewVWHpvfvlIlI5PfeCn1yOVjDS',
  'sequenceReference': {'type': 'SequenceReference',
   'refgetAccession': 'SQ.ItRDD47aMoioDCNW_occY5fWKZBKlxCX'},
  'start': [11211021, 11213338],
  'end': [11217364, 11218067]},
 'copyChange': 'gain'}

Note the coordinate shift: HGVS uses 1-based inclusive coordinates, VRS uses 0-based interbase. For the outer-left side, each boundary becomes N - 1; for the outer-right side, the boundaries are preserved. So (11211022_11213339) on the start side becomes [11211021, 11213338].

items.title: Example 5 — VRS → HGVS (round-trip)
items.text:
A VRS Allele whose SequenceLocation has Range bounds can be serialized back to uncertain-range HGVS via AlleleTranslator.from_vrs. Here we build the Allele directly (since from_hgvs on the Allele path refuses uncertain ranges) and confirm it round-trips.

In [6]
allele = models.Allele(
    location=models.SequenceLocation(
        sequenceReference=models.SequenceReference(
            refgetAccession="SQ.pnAqCRBrTsUoBghSD1yp_jXWSmlbdh4g"  # NC_000002.12
        ),
        start=models.Range(root=[None, 202376934]),
        end=models.Range(root=[202377551, 202464808]),
    ),
    state=models.LiteralSequenceExpression(sequence=models.sequenceString(root="")),
)
allele_tlr.from_vrs(allele, "hgvs")

Output:

['NC_000002.12:g.(?_202376935)_(202377551_202464808)del']

items.title: Example 6 — Why not AlleleTranslator.from_hgvs for uncertain ranges?
items.text:
An Allele carries a concrete LiteralSequenceExpression (or similar) state. When breakpoints are uncertain, the reference sequence at the variant boundaries is unknown, so a literal sequence state is ill-defined. The translator raises a clear error and points you to CnvTranslator.

In [7]
try:
    allele_tlr.to_vrs(
        "NC_000019.9:g.(11211022_11213339)_(11217364_11218067)dup", "hgvs"
    )
except ValueError as err:
    print(type(err).__name__, ":", err)

Output:

ValueError : Uncertain-range HGVS expressions are not supported for Allele translation; use CnvTranslator for del/dup
